sanskrit: yajñapatim ṛṣaya enasāhur nirbhaktā bhāgād anutapyamānāḥ | yad enaś cakṛvān baddha eṣa tato viśvakarman pra mumugdhy enam ||
english: The seers declare the lord of the sacrifice to be guilty of sin — those excluded from their portion, consumed with grief. Inasmuch as he has committed this wrong, being bound by it — from that, O Viśvakarman, release him.

sanskrit: adānyān somapān manyamāno yajñasya vidvān samaye na dhīraḥ | madhavyān stokān apa yān rarādha saṃ mā taiḥ sṛjatu viśvakarmā ||
english: Deeming those who should not have drunk the soma as drinkers, knowing the rite yet not steady at the proper time — the sweet drops which he has withheld: may Viśvakarman unite me with them.

sanskrit: ye bhakṣayanto na vasūny ānṛdhur yān agnayo anvatapyanta dhiṣṇyāḥ | yā teṣām avayā duriṣṭāt sviṣṭaṃ tad viśvakarmā kṛṇotu ||
english: Those who, while consuming, did not prosper the good things — whom the altar fires have burned after — the expiation of theirs for a wrongly performed sacrifice: may Viśvakarman make that a well-performed one.

sanskrit: bhīmā ṛṣayo namo astv ebhyaś cakṣur yad eṣāṃ manasaś ca saṃdṛk | bṛhaspataye mahiṣāya dive namo viśvakarman namas te pāhy asmān ||
english: Awe-inspiring are the seers — homage be to them, for their eye and the insight of their mind. To Bṛhaspati, to the great bull, to Heaven — homage. O Viśvakarman, homage to you; protect us.

sanskrit: sarvā imā oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyām adhi niṣṭhitāḥ | athaiva bhadrike tvam asurebhyo ajāyathāḥ ||
english: All these plants are established upon the earth. Even so, O auspicious one, you were born from the Asuras.

sanskrit: śataṃ jahy apsarasāṃ śataṃ śvanvatīnām | gandharvapatnīnāṃ śatasya- -indro api kṛtac chiraḥ ||
english: Strike down a hundred of the Apsarases, a hundred of those accompanied by dogs; of the hundred wives of the Gandharvas — Indra has even cut off their heads.

sanskrit: yāḥ patanti puro vātaṃ patanti reṣmabhiḥ saha | cetantīm aśmalāṃ palām indro apsaraso hanat ||
english: Those who fly ahead of the wind, who fly together with storms — the waking Aśmalā, the Palā: Indra has slain those Apsarases.

sanskrit: vi vo yaśo havāmahe vi vo haviṣyam odanam | apāvarīr aporṇuta- -asmad yakṣmaṃ aporṇuta vātas tejanyaṃ yathā ||
english: We call away your fame, we call away your oblation-rice. Uncover, strip away — strip the disease from us, as the wind strips the seed-bearing plant.

sanskrit: asitasya vidradhasya lohitasya vanaspate | visalpakasyauṣadhe moc chiṣaḥ piśitaṃ cana ||
english: Of the dark abscess, the vidradha, the blood-red one, O lord of the forest; O herb of the visalpaka — do not leave behind even a shred of flesh.

sanskrit: yat te balāsa tiṣṭhataḥ kakṣe muṣkāv apākṛtam | vedāhaṃ tasya bheṣajaṃ cīpadrām abhicakṣaṇam ||
english: What balāsa stands in the armpit of one standing, removed from the testicles — I know the remedy for that: the cīpadrā plant for beholding it.

sanskrit: nir balāsaṃ balāsino visalpam uta vidradham | paropahatyāṃ te vayaṃ parā yakṣmaṃ suvāmasi ||
english: The balāsa from the one afflicted with balāsa, the visalpa and also the vidradha — through the counter-strike, we drive your disease away, we press it far off.

sanskrit: śīrṣarogam aṅgarogaṃ śuktivalgaṃ vilohitam | parā te ajñātaṃ yakṣmaṃ adharāñcaṃ suvāmasi ||
english: The sickness of the head, the sickness of the limbs, the śuktivalga, the blood-red disease — your unknown wasting disease we press downward and away.
